acceptanceCriteria.text: The state runtime shall expose exactly one documented bootstrap entrypoint that creates the initial `{workflow-id}.state.md` and `{workflow-id}.state.json` pair for a new run.
When the bootstrap entrypoint runs, the state runtime shall require a workflow id, a slug, a branch, and a baseline commit, and shall reject a branch value of `HEAD`.
The bootstrap entrypoint shall write the JSON member of the pair as machine source of truth and the Markdown member as its render, both inside `{us-dir}` under the configured plans directory.

The bootstrap entrypoint shall write `stateVersion` 3, `revision` 0, `workflowType` for the invoked pipeline, `status` `active`, and `currentStep` 0, with the workflow id, slug, branch, and baseline recorded in the same record.
When the bootstrap entrypoint completes, the written record shall satisfy `validateSnapshot` without any further write or recovery command.
When the bootstrap gives the entrypoint an empty or absent plans index, the entrypoint shall create the index and its workflow row so the row `stateSha256` matches the written pair.
The bootstrap entrypoint shall record a machine-readable result naming the workflow id, both written paths, and the resolved plans index.

While a bootstrapped state pair at revision 0 has no dispatch, the bootstrap entrypoint shall leave both files byte-identical on a repeated run and report the replay as idempotent with a zero exit code.
If the target state path already holds a record at revision greater than 0, then the bootstrap entrypoint shall refuse with a non-zero exit code and leave every file unchanged.
If the target state path already holds a record whose `completedSteps` is non-empty, then the bootstrap entrypoint shall refuse with a non-zero exit code and leave every file unchanged.
If the target state path already holds a record whose `status` is terminal, then the bootstrap entrypoint shall refuse with a non-zero exit code and leave every file unchanged.
If exactly one member of the state pair is present at the target path, then the bootstrap entrypoint shall fail closed with a non-zero exit code and name the missing member.
If a required flag value is empty, or the baseline is not a commit-shaped hexadecimal string, then the bootstrap entrypoint shall reject the invocation with a usage error.
If the slug fails to match the plan directory name, then the bootstrap entrypoint shall refuse the write and name the mismatch.
If the workflow id departs from the documented `{slug}-{ISO8601}` shape, then the bootstrap entrypoint shall refuse the write and quote the expected shape.
The bootstrap entrypoint shall leave no partial pair and no index row behind when it fails, so a failed invocation leaves any pre-existing state byte-identical.
When the state runtime is invoked with `--help`, the help output shall list the bootstrap usage line with a sample invocation.
Where the bootstrap path is documented, the contract text shall state the bootstrap command, the pair invariant, the idempotent replay rule, and the refusal rules in one canonical section.
The bootstrap path shall execute on Node 22 with CommonJS `.cjs` modules, and the repository shall require no Python interpreter for it.
The verification command set shall include the bootstrap path and its refusal behaviors as an automated test module registered in `test/test-suites.json`.
The bootstrap entrypoint shall write only repo-relative paths into the state record and shall emit no absolute machine path.

negativeScenarios.text: Red test: bootstrap over a state whose `revision` is 3 and assert a non-zero exit with both members byte-identical afterwards; before this contract the same invocation is impossible (the operation is rejected) and the hand-edit remains the only path.
Red test: bootstrap over a state with a non-empty `completedSteps` and assert refusal, so an already-running or finished run is never re-initialized.
Red test: bootstrap with only `{workflow-id}.state.md` on disk and assert a fail-closed error naming the missing JSON member, with no file created.
Red test: bootstrap with an empty slug and assert a usage error and no write; repeat with `--branch HEAD` and with a baseline that is not a hexadecimal commit string.
Red test: bootstrap with a slug whose value differs from the plan directory name and assert refusal naming the mismatch.
Red test: bootstrap with a workflow id outside the `{slug}-{ISO8601}` shape and assert refusal quoting the expected shape.
Red test: bootstrap with the plans directory absent and assert the command still creates the index row, so `validate_state.cjs` resolves the workflow instead of failing on a missing index entry.

Red test: bootstrap, dispatch Step 0 through `update_state.cjs`, then re-run bootstrap and assert refusal (the run has progressed), proving the idempotent window is genuinely limited to the untouched revision-0 pair.
Red test: simulate a failed write (unwritable plans directory) and assert no partial pair and no index row remain, and that a pre-existing state is byte-identical afterwards.

Stack invariant negative test: run the bootstrap and its test module under `node` with no Python on the path and assert both pass, proving the Node 22 CommonJS-only invariant; a `.py` helper introduced anywhere under `.agents/skills/` or `bin/` must fail `ws-check-harness`.
Regression assertion: re-run the existing state suites and assert the dispatch/finish/checkpoint semantics, the telemetry event schema, and the plans-index hash comparison behave exactly as before.
Contract assertion: assert the canonical bootstrap section states the pair invariant, the replay rule, and the refusal rules, and that the runtime `--help` output lists the bootstrap usage line.
